page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-32 is a compute-focused instance type within the first-generation N1 family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and features a 2.3 GHz Intel Xeon processor providing 32 vCPUs across 16 dedicated physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 0.25 MB L2 cache per core, and a 45 MB shared L3 cache. Memory is provisioned at 29.0 GB, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of roughly 0.9 GB per vCPU. The server includes no bundled local NVMe storage and has no hardware accelerators or GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a significant divergence between single-thread throughput and parallel compute capacity. Single-core tests show weaker metrics, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring 1116.39 and Geekbench single-core reaching 954.0, both placing in the bottom 25%. Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression fall into the bottom 10%. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics perform squarely within the middle 50% across industry baselines. Geekbench multi-core registers at 8521.0, stress-ng multi-core achieves 23469.51, and the PassMark CPU score reaches 22235.88. Static web serving reaches 17.77 GB/sec, while Redis SET operations achieve 21.44 million operations per second.

Hardware vectorization support includes AVX and AES instructions, but lacks newer extensions such as AVX-512, AMX, and SHA-NI. Consequently, AI workloads are heavily constrained, with 135M-parameter LLM inference executing at only 159.91 prompt tokens/sec and 8.94 generation tokens/sec, placing in the bottom 10%. Memory throughput remains stable for its generation, recording 94.87 GB/sec large-block read bandwidth and 43.85 GB/sec write bandwidth.

The qualitative profile of n1-highcpu-32 delivers high thread concurrency where per-core raw clock latency is not critical. It is well matched for distributed batch computation, multi-threaded code compilation (Clang score of 18014.0), ray tracing, and horizontal microservices that require significant core density over memory volume. It is not suitable for large in-memory databases, memory-heavy data pipelines, or accelerated machine learning inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-32 is a compute-oriented virtual machine configuration powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. It provisions 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores with hyper-threading) and 29.0 GB of RAM, resulting in approximately 0.9 GB of memory per thread. The instance does not bundle local storage or GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate solid middle-tier multi-threaded throughput, registering 23469.51 in stress-ng multi-core and 8521.0 in Geekbench multi-core, alongside 18014.0 in Clang compilation tests. However, single-core processing and tasks lacking thread scalability exhibit weaker performance, ranking in the bottom 25% or lower. The server also lacks AVX-512 and modern matrix instruction extensions, limiting its utility for machine learning inference. It provides an efficient resource footprint for parallel batch tasks, CI/CD code compilation, and thread-intensive web or microservice serving that does not require large memory arrays.
